title noun

of a person: a name of rank or honour

also titles, job title, honorific, form of address

classical

Cic. Att. 5.20.4: appellātiōne hāc inānī
Traupman 395

appellātiō, appellātiōnis f.

noun, third declension · Declension on Wiktionary

a name, title

A calling by name, and so the name or title one is called by. Its other classical senses are an address to someone and, in law, an appeal (to the tribunes, Cic. Quinct. 64).

Other words

  • titulus, titulī m. — title of honour; glory

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. Pis. 19: sustinēre titulum cōnsulātūs (Lewis & Short); Hor. S. 1.6.17 (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    A title as a mark of honour (titulus cōnsulātūs), not a form of address; also the title of a book (see title, of a book).

  • mūneris titulus — job title

    also used · Renaissance · M-O s.v. title (professional), citing Milton (1674)

Examples

  • vēnit interim Bibulus; crēdō, voluit appellātiōne hāc inānī nōbīs esse pār.

    Meanwhile Bibulus arrived; I suppose he wanted to be my equal in this empty title.Cic. Att. 5.20.4

See also title, name.
